privacy.title: Privacy Notice
description: This website is designed to collect as little information as possible. The data it
collect is used to identify which chess lines and topics are frequently viewed, so that new or updated content
can focus on those areas. It will
be shared with any third parties.
The site does not use advertisements, third-party analytics, or cookies.
When the page is loaded, it creates a random session ID. This is replaced with a new random ID each time
the page is reloaded, and is not used to recognise returning visitors.
During a session, the website may record:

value: The actions of loading the page, making or undoing moves on the chess board (this includes clicking
any buttons which make or undo moves on the board), or opening a glossary topic
, and any moves stored in the
Some additional non-identifying metadata (specifically, the HTTP method and API route of requests
sent by the page, and the page URL)

description: This information is used only to understand how visitors interact with the site's content, with the goal of
improving it.
Like pretty much every other website on the internet, this site necessarily processes technical information
(such as your IP address) in order to operate; in this case, that technical information is used to deliver web pages
to your browser, to notify the browser if the site has updated, and to collect the data listed above. It is
intentionally stored beyond those purposes. The server is specifically configured not to generate its standard access
logs for visits to the site.
The site is hosted by a third-party provider, which also necessarily processes technical information
required to deliver the website. Unfortunately, I can't control what data they store.
As is stated in the
section, this project is open source. If you're interested in how the site collects data, please feel free to
inspect the code.

welcome.title: Welcome to Cogit
description: The goal of this project is to function as a comprehensive resource for chess improvement. Its contents are
written and edited to be concise, without omitting important details, and approachable even to beginners.
It's assumed that the reader knows the rules of the game, but nothing beyond that is required.
Individual moves are referenced using
, which is standard practice in the chess world.
Each time a move is played on the interactive chess board, relevant information is added to the
box directly above this article.

value: All commentary is written manually move-by-move, to ensure that it is high quality. Due to the exponential
nature of chess, only a small fraction of all possible move sequences can be covered this way, so the
available commentary focuses mostly on common openings, notable games, and some additional short branches from those points.

description: The
segment just underneath the chess board displays possible moves in the current board position
which have commentary available (or which lead to later moves with commentary).
The segment in which
is displayed is the
. In order to keep commentary for individual moves short, detailed explanations of concepts are separated out into
glossary topics, which can be accessed using the margin to the left.
If a glossary topic is relevant or necessary to understand a move, a button to open that topic will also be present
in the move's commentary.
This layout is designed to make it easy to get started - play moves on the chess board, read through the
commentary, and click on embedded buttons to learn more about any unfamiliar concepts.
